newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end lower on Sammi Group's failure.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end lower on Sammi Group's failure.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed lower in Saturday's half-day session as the Sammi Group's woes continued to reverberate through the share market, brokers said.
The composite stock index shed 4.50 points to 623.13.

"Investors are not easily recovering from the Sammi shock," said broker Hong Jong-hyun of Coryo Securities. "Major concerns focused on the possibility of a domino effect of more defaults in line with tightening liquidity."

Jitters over failures among affiliates of the conglomerate had hit financial shares hard in recent days. But they rebounded on Saturday as investors apparently believed prices had fallen too far already, brokers said.
The financial sub-index rose 3.73 percent or 16.05 points to 445.91.
"No one thinks the government will let domestic financial institutions go bust," Hong said, based on the belief that financial share prices were too cheap.
Korea First Bank, which fell to a year low of 2,670 on Friday, went limit up to 2,880. The bank is the major creditor to insolvent Sammi Steel.
Commercial Bank of Korea added 160 won to 3,600 after briefly hitting a year low of 3,440.
